bibl.title: Reactivation of hippocampal ensemble memories during sleep

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: hippocampal ensemble reactivation during sleep
span.quote: On the hypothesis that hippocampal activity during sleep reflects the reactivation of population events representing the experiences of the prior waking behavior, cell pairs that were coactive during the RUN phase (because of their place field overlap) were examined during the POST phase and compared with cell pairs that were active but not coactive during behavior (non-overlapping place fields) (Figs. 2 and 3).

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: With the use of multielectrcde recording techniques (4), the activity of 50 to 100 single cells in area CAI of the hippocampus was monitored simultaneously during sleep periods before and after brief behavioral episodes (Fig. 1).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Waking experience drives associative synaptic modification, which leaves cells that were coactive during behaviour more likely to be reactivated together in subsequent slow-wave sleep
span.quote: This effect, which declined gradually during each post-behaviorsleep session, may resultfrom synaptic modificationduringwaking experience.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Event memory is first stored by rapid synaptic modification in the hippocampus, and is then replayed during slow-wave sleep (when further hippocampal modification is suppressed) so that the information is gradually transferred to neocortex
span.quote: During subsequent slow-wave sleep, synaptic moditication within the hippocampus itself is suppressed (16) and the neuronal states encoded within the hippocampus are "played back" as part of a consolidation process by which hippocampal information is gradually transferred to, the neocortex (6, 17).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Initial storage of the event occurs through rapid synaptic modification primarily within the hippocampus itself
span.quote: According to the proposed hypothesis, initial storage of event memory occurs through rapid synaptic modification, primarily within the hippocampus.

span.label: The increased correlation implies associative synaptic change somewhere in the system, but not necessarily inside the hippocampus.
span.quote: The inaeased melation is consistent with an underlying associative synaptic modification at some stage in the system, although not necessarily in the hippocampus.

span.label: Neocortical or subcortical changes are an alternative source of the increased correlations.
span.quote: Changes in neocortical or subcortical pathways might underlie the increased correlations.

span.label: builds-on → previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (ref. 6)
span.quote: This difTerence is consistent with previous theoretical models of autoassociative memory (6), in which recurrent excitation is used to reproduce a previously stored activity pattern, even when the input contains very little of the relevant information.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: Cells that were correlated (OVR, solid bars) during the RUN phase exhibited a significant (analysis of variance, P < 0.05) increase in correlation during the post-run (POST) sleep relative to pre-run (PRE) sleep (*) or to cells that were non-overlapped (NON, hollow bars), and hence uncorrelated during running (plus signs).

span.label: cross-correlation
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: mean
span.quote: Mean crosscorrelations (2100 ms) for cell pairs during PRE, RUN, and POST phases (Fig. 2).

span.label: Hippocampal CA1 cells that fired together during a spatial behavioural task showed increased tendency to fire together in the sleep that followed, relative to the sleep that preceded the task.
span.quote: Cells that fired together when the animal occupied particular locations in the environment exhibitedan increasedtendencyto fire together duringsubsequent sleep, in comparison to sleep episodes precedingthe behavioraltasks.

span.label: The increase was specific to coactive pairs: cells silent during behaviour, and active cells whose place fields did not overlap, showed no such increase.
span.quote: Cells that were inactive during behavior, or that were active but had non-overlappingspatial firing, did not show this increase.

span.label: Coactive (overlapping place field) pairs rose significantly above their pre-behaviour correlation level, whereas pairs of spatially firing cells with non-overlapping fields did not.
span.quote: Cells that were coactive during behavior showed a significant increase in correlation from their PRE level compared to pairs in which both cells displayed spatial firing but not in the same region of space (11).

span.label: The reactivation effect decayed across the post-behaviour sleep session with a time constant of about 12 minutes.
span.quote: This selective reactivation of correlated states declined during the POST phase with a time constant of approximately 12 min (1 2).

span.label: The sleep correlations were concentrated in the synchronized population bursts (ripples) rather than in the intervals between them.
span.quote: Correlations were signiiicantly larger during ripples than in the intervening intervals (14).

span.label: During running, cells with overlapping place fields were strongly positively correlated while non-overlapping pairs were not, confirming the grouping used for the sleep comparison.
span.quote: During the RUN phase, as expected, cells with overlapping place fields exhibited highly positively correlated activity, whereas cell pairs with nonoverlapping fields did not exhibit such activity (Fig. 3).

span.label: ripples (synchronized population bursts of slow-wave sleep)
span.term: ripples (synchronized population bursts of slow-wave sleep)
span.quote: During slow-wave sleep, cells discharge in intermittent, synchronized bursts (ripples) (9), associated with electroencephalogram (EEG) sharp-wave (SPW) activity.

span.label: recording phase (pre-behavioural sleep, running, post-behavioural sleep)
span.term: recording phase (pre-behavioural sleep, running, post-behavioural sleep)
span.quote: Spike-train cross-correlations were computed for all pairs of principal cells during the pre-behavioral sleep (PRE) , running (RUN), and post-behavioral sleep (POST) periods.

span.label: amount of spatial (place-field) overlap between the two cells of a pair
span.term: amount of spatial (place-field) overlap between the two cells of a pair
span.quote: Cell pairs were grouped on the basis of the amount of overlap between their spatial firing distributions.

span.label: short-latency cross-correlation of the two cells' spike trains
span.term: short-latency cross-correlation of the two cells' spike trains
span.quote: For each cell pair, the short latency (A 100 ms) cross-correlation of spike trains was computed over each period (8); each period was approximately 20 min in duration (9).

span.label: significant spatial firing on the apparatus (inclusion criterion holding place-cell status constant across the compared groups)
span.term: significant spatial firing on the apparatus (inclusion criterion holding place-cell status constant across the compared groups)
span.quote: Only cells with significant spatial firing on the apparatus are included (10).

span.label: approximately 12 min — time constant of the decay of the reactivated correlation during post-behaviour sleep
span.quote: This selective reactivation of correlated states declined during the POST phase with a time constant of approximately 12 min (1 2).

span.label: rat 1: 49 cells; rat 2: 74 cells; rat 3: 69 cells — number of simultaneously recorded hippocampal pyramidal cells in each of the three rats
span.quote: Spatial firing characteristics of populations of simultaneously recorded hippocampal pyramidal cells from three rats (rat 1: 49 cells; rat 2: 74 cells; rat 3: 69 cells).

span.label: 50 to 100 — number of single CA1 cells monitored simultaneously in each recording session
span.quote: With the use of multielectrcde recording techniques (4), the activity of 50 to 100 single cells in area CAI of the hippocampus was monitored simultaneously during sleep periods before and after brief behavioral episodes (Fig. 1).

span.label: NON 437 and OVR 60; NON 719 and OVR 95; NON 941 and OVR 147 — numbers of non-overlapping versus overlapping cell pairs contributing to the histograms for rats 1, 2 and 3
span.quote: The numbers of cell pairs contributing to each histogram were as follows: (A) Rat 1, NON 437 and OVR 60; (B) Rat 2, NON 719 and OVR 95; (C) Rat 3, NON 941 and OVR 147.

span.label: P < 0.05 — significance level at which the post-run correlation increase for coactive pairs was established by ANOVA
span.quote: Cells that were correlated (OVR, solid bars) during the RUN phase exhibited a significant (analysis of variance, P < 0.05) increase in correlation during the post-run (POST) sleep relative to pre-run (PRE) sleep (*) or to cells that were non-overlapped (NON, hollow bars), and hence uncorrelated during running (plus signs).

span.label: approximately 20 min — duration of each of the PRE, RUN and POST recording periods
span.quote: For each cell pair, the short latency (A 100 ms) cross-correlation of spike trains was computed over each period (8); each period was approximately 20 min in duration (9).
